chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I am at the Scale on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever's evil deeds are heavier than his good deeds, I will bring the salutations upon me by him so that I may make his good deeds heavier with them.'

key_terms.الْمِيزَانِ: The Scale of Deeds on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: How does the Prophet Muhammad help balance the scales for those with more sins than good deeds?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the intercessory role of the Prophet (s.a.w.s.) on the Day of Judgment, where he personally stands by the Mizan to weigh the merits of his followers. By incorporating the recited Salawaat as a spiritual weight, the Prophet ensures that the devotion of the believers tips the scale in their favor, emphasizing the practical efficacy of love and remembrance in achieving salvation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s active involvement in the cosmic accounting, linking personal piety directly to divine mercy.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam   Muhammad   Baqir   (a.s.)   narrates   from   his predecessors  that  the  Holy  Prophet  (s.a.w.s.)  said,  “I  will stand near Mizan on the Day of Judgment. If I see a person whose sins are more than his good deeds I will keep the salutations recited on me by him in the pan of good deeds and make it tilt in his favor.”
